$comment: Why this case is in the corpus: scoreRun used to rebuild its per-criterion lookup with `new Map([...reportedCriteria]
.map(...))`, keyed by stripped name. Two report headings that strip to the same name collapse into one Map entry, and
since a later `.set()` on the same key overwrites the earlier one, only the LAST heading's citations survived; the
earlier heading's were discarded with nothing recorded that they ever existed. A peer review of Story 8.1, run
before this PR opened, found the dangerous direction: if the first (discarded) heading carried a real but wrong
citation and the second (surviving) heading carried the correct one, the wrong citation was never examined and the
criterion scored fully grounded, exactly the outcome AC1 says a real-but-irrelevant citation must not produce.
The report is CONSTRUCTED: gapped-correct-audit's report with its single `### Compliance` heading split into two,
`### Compliance (SOC 2)` (citing `evidence/load-test-2026-08-28.json`, a real file in the bundle but not one
ground truth declares for Compliance) followed by `### Compliance (GDPR)` (citing the already-correct
`evidence/security-review-2026-08-29.md`), and nothing else touched. Both strip to `Compliance`.
The fix concatenates rather than overwrites: `byStrippedName` now collects every real citation from every heading
that strips to a given name, so the wrong citation from the first heading is examined alongside the correct one
from the second, and `real.every(...)` (the every()-not-some() fix from the same commit) catches it.
Reverting to the overwriting Map and replaying this case fails it: groundedCriteria moves from {16,17} to {17,17}
and ungroundedCitations empties, silently hiding the wrong citation, which is the regression this case exists to
derivation: One criterion's single heading was split into two, one file moved to the new first heading, and nothing else
changed, so every status, count and ceiling below not touching Compliance is gapped-correct-audit's own.
Statuses, coverage, thresholds, overall, unknownThreshold and cleanFalsePositives: identical to gapped-correct-audit,
since none of those readers touch Compliance's own citations.
Citations: security now carries six entries where gapped-correct-audit carries five, evidence/load-test-2026-08-28.json
inserted where Compliance's heading sits (the fifth of six citations kept its position; the new one lands right
before it). That file is real (already cited under Performance), so fabricated stays empty.
Grounding: sixteen of the seventeen criteria with declared evidence are grounded. Compliance is the miss: its two
headings, `Compliance (SOC 2)` and `Compliance (GDPR)`, both strip to `Compliance` and their citations are
concatenated rather than the second overwriting the first, so the real citations scored are
evidence/load-test-2026-08-28.json (from the first heading, not one of the two files ground truth declares for
Compliance) and evidence/security-review-2026-08-29.md (from the second, and correct). real.every() fails on the
